paragraphs: Children in care in Cambridgeshire are looked after by Cambridgeshire County Council's own fostering service and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. In December 2024 the council said it had high numbers of children in its care, a shortage of foster carers and many children waiting for a foster home, and that it urgently needed more carers.

The council is part of Foster East, which brings together councils across the east of England. Foster East has said there are around 7,000 children in care in the region, with roughly a classroom's worth more coming into care every week. Some need a home for only a few weeks, for example while a parent is ill or unable to look after them; others need a family for much longer.

To foster with the council you need to be over 21, and there is no upper age limit. You can be single or in a couple, own or rent your home, have children or pets of your own, and work full-time or part-time or foster full-time. The council says its training and support networks are delivered locally. It does not publish its allowance rates in its news releases, so ask for the current figures when you enquire.

Agencies set their own fees and support, so it is worth speaking to the council and two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you choose.

sources.title: You could change the life of a child in Cambridgeshire by becoming a foster carer (Cambridgeshire County Council, December 2024)
